blocks.content: Quiz: How would you style an anchor element in CSS such that it changes color on hover?
Tap an option below to answer:

a { color: red; } 
a:hover { color: green; }
The :hover pseudo-class is used to style elements when a user hovers over them.
The :hover pseudo-class is used to style elements when a user hovers over them.

a { color: red; } 
a:active { color: green; }
The :active pseudo-class styles an element when a user presses and holds a mouse button on it, not when they hover over it.
The :active pseudo-class styles an element when a user presses and holds a mouse button on it, not when they hover over it.

a { color: red; } 
a:visited { color: green; }
The :visited pseudo-class is used for links that have been visited, not for general changes upon hovering.
The :visited pseudo-class is used for links that have been visited, not for general changes upon hovering.

a { color: red; } 
a:first-child { color: green; }
The :first-child pseudo-class targets the first child of its parent element; it doesn't implement hovering.
The :first-child pseudo-class targets the first child of its parent element; it doesn't implement hovering.
